title: A River Reveals Its Roman Past

parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: A River Reveals its Roman Past
parts.article:
A River Reveals its Roman Past

(A) 2,000 years ago, the town of Arles, in what is now south-western France, was a busy gateway to the area of the Roman Empire known as Gaul. Goods from all over the Mediterranean were transferred there to barges – long, shallow riverboats – then pulled up the Rhône river to supply the northern half of the great empire. Today, Arles is a small, quiet place, and the Rhône is polluted and mostly ignored.

(B) Archaeologist Luc Long is a native of Arles. He had already worked on sunken ships all over the Mediterranean when, in 1986, a friend persuaded him to dive for the first time in his home river. Long reluctantly agreed. The two men entered the river on a chilly November morning, when the water was around 8°C, thick, cloudy and foul-smelling. They could see no more than a metre ahead through the murky water. At a depth of about six metres, Long saw a sunken truck. To his surprise, he discovered an ancient Roman jar – known as an amphora – on the driver’s seat. These containers were used throughout the Roman Empire to transport olive oil, fish sauce, and other products. When empty, they would simply be discarded. Within a short time the divers found themselves swimming over a vast field of amphorae. Long had never seen so many intact ones, and he has been mapping this Roman rubbish dump ever since.

(C) For the first 20 years or so, no one paid much attention to what Long was doing. When, in 2004, one of his colleagues came across a 34-metre-long Roman barge, Long doubted that there would ever be enough money available to raise it. In 2007, Long handed over the study of this wreck – which he named Arles-Rhône 3 – to three younger archaeologists, and continued his survey of the rest of the dump, around 50 metres upstream. This was where he started finding pieces of the Roman town of Arles, including statues. Word began to leak out. The French customs police warned Long that antiquities thieves might be watching his operation. So when his divers found a two-metre statue of the god Neptune, they brought it to the surface at night.

(D) Before the diving season was over, divers had discovered a rare marble bust of the Roman emperor Julius Caesar. An exhibition was built around the statue, and news of it spread around the world. ‘The exhibition’s success was astonishing,’ said Claude Sintes, director of Arles’ local antiquities museum, where the exhibition was held. ‘When a modest town like ours gets 400,000 visitors, the politicians understood that the economic return was strong.’ By the autumn of 2010, the Caesar exhibition was nearing its end, and some politicians were looking for more culture to invest in, because the European Union had designated the region around Arles a 2013 European Capital of Culture. Suddenly nine million euros became available to build a new wing on the museum and put a Roman barge into it. There was just one small problem. The project would need to be completed by 2013. That meant the barge needed to be extracted by the end of the diving season in 2011. This was because although the wood of the boat had suffered no microbial decay, water had filled its cells, leaving the whole structure soft and spongy. If that were to evaporate, the boat would collapse. The solution was to bathe the wood for months in a polymer called polyethylene glycol, then freeze-dry it in small sections – gradually infusing it with the polymer before extracting the water. The process would take nearly two years.

(E) So there was only one diving season to extract the boat from the Rhône. ‘We thought the project was doomed to fail,’ said Benoît Poinard, a professional diver and the site foreman. Normally, Poinard explained, the Rhône is safe for diving only from late June to October; otherwise the current is too strong. Only three or four months would not be enough to excavate Arles-Rhône 3. Then 2011 arrived. It hardly snowed in the Alps that winter and that spring it barely rained. The Rhône’s current was so gentle that the team got in the water by early May. The team worked straight into November, losing only a single week to bad weather – and completed the job. ‘Two hours after we finished,’ Poinard said, ‘the Rhône became undiveable for the whole winter.’

(F) When Arles-Rhône 3 sank, it was carrying 33 tons of stone for building work. It had come from a quarry just north of Arles, and was probably heading towards a construction site further down the river. The boat was pointed upstream, though, rather than downstream, indicating it had been moored at the quay when it sank. A flash flood had probably swamped it. As soon as the flood subsided, the barge would have been covered in a coating of fine clay no more than 20 cm thick. This was where the archaeologists discovered the personal effects that the crew had left on the boat, including cooking utensils and plates. When the restorers were taking the boat apart, they also found a silver coin sealed between two planks of wood; it had been put there to bring good luck. And it did – 2,000 years later. Arles-Rhône 3 was able to take its place in the new wing of the museum, on schedule, just over two years after re-emerging from the cloudy depths of the Rhône.

questions.question: In 1986 Luc Long had been looking for an opportunity to dive in the Rhone for some time.

analyses.content: 原文说Long是被朋友劝说才第一次去罗讷河潜水，并且是“勉强同意（reluctantly agreed）”，与题目说的“他一直在寻找机会潜水”完全相反。
你可能会把他在地中海其他地方的潜水经历误认为是他在罗讷河找机会，注意区分地点。
He had already worked on sunken ships all over the Mediterranean when, in 1986, a friend persuaded him to dive for the first time in his home river. Long reluctantly agreed.

questions.question: Long and his friend were the first divers to find Roman remains in the Rhone.

analyses.content: 原文只说了Long和朋友潜水时惊讶地发现了古罗马罐子，但并没有提到他们是不是“第一批（first divers）”在这里发现古罗马遗迹的人。
你可能看到他们发现了文物就觉得他们是第一人，但不要自行脑补原文没有给出的“第一”这个概念。
At a depth of about six metres, Long saw a sunken truck. To his surprise, he discovered an ancient Roman jar – known as an amphora – on the driver’s seat.

questions.question: Long's work in the Rhone attracted immediate interest.

analyses.content: 原文明确说在最初的大约20年里，根本没人关注他在做什么，直接反驳了题目中的“立刻引起了兴趣（immediate interest）”。
如果你看到后面的段落提到展览很成功，那是很多年之后的事情，千万不要张冠李戴。
For the first 20 years or so, no one paid much attention to what Long was doing.

questions.question: It was thought that the Neptune statue would be of interest to thieves.

analyses.content: 原文提到法国海关警察警告Long可能会有文物盗贼盯着他们，所以他们选择在夜间把海神雕像打捞上来，这说明雕像确实会引起盗贼的兴趣。
你可能在找“thought”这个词的直接替换，但“警察警告有盗贼”以及“夜间打捞”的实际行动，已经完美印证了题目里的意思。

The French customs police warned Long that antiquities thieves might be watching his operation. So when his divers found a two-metre statue of the god Neptune, they brought it to the surface at night.

questions.question: Benoit Poinard doubted that the barge could be raised in one diving season.

analyses.content: 原文写道，只有唯一的一个潜水季来打捞这艘船，而Benoît Poinard直接说“我们以为这个项目注定要失败”，完全符合题目中他对一个潜水季内完成打捞表示怀疑的说法。
不要被“doomed to fail（注定失败）”吓到，这就是对应题目中“doubted（怀疑）”能否成功的直接体现。
So there was only one diving season to extract the boat from the Rhône. ‘We thought the project was doomed to fail,’ said Benoît Poinard, a professional diver and the site foreman.

questions.question: The restorers were surprised to discover a silver coin in the barge.

analyses.content: 原文提到了修复人员在两块木板之间找到了一枚银币，但完全没有提到他们对这个发现是否感到“惊讶（surprised）”。
你可能会因为发现了好东西就主观认为他们肯定很惊讶，切记做NOT GIVEN题时不能加入个人情感推断。
When the restorers were taking the boat apart, they also found a silver coin sealed between two planks of wood; it had been put there to bring good luck.

groups.description:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–6 on your answer sheet, write.

groups.contentHtml:
The Roman barge Arles-Rhone 3
The discovery and condition of the barge:
• The barge was 34 metres long and was found by one of Long’s in 2004.
• The wood had not decayed, but water had filled its cells, making the structure soft and .
Extraction from the Rhone:
• Normally, the Rhone is safe for diving only from late June to .
• In 2011, because it hardly snowed in the Alps, the river’s was very gentle.
• The diving team lost only one to bad weather.
What was found on or near the barge:
• The barge was carrying 33 tons of for building work.
• Under the floorboards, restorers found a silver dated to 30 BCE.

analyses.content: 题目问这艘船在2004年是被Long的什么人发现的，原文直接给出了“one of his colleagues（他的一位同事）”，提取名词即可。
定位时看准时间2004年，不要错填成前面的friend，因为那是1986年的事情。
When, in 2004, one of his colleagues came across a 34-metre-long Roman barge, Long doubted that there would ever be enough money available to raise it.
题目需要填一个和soft并列的形容词，原文中直接用“soft and spongy”给出了答案。
你可能会去关注前面的decay，但题目中的but已经转折了，往后找并列连词and后面的词最稳妥。
This was because although the wood of the boat had suffered no microbial decay, water had filled its cells, leaving the whole structure soft and spongy.
题目问罗讷河通常在哪两个月之间适合潜水，原文直接说是“from late June to October”，照抄月份单词即可。
找准“safe for diving”这个核心条件，不要和后面提到实际打捞时的May或November混淆。
Normally, Poinard explained, the Rhône is safe for diving only from late June to October; otherwise the current is too strong.
题目问2011年河流的什么非常gentle，原文写的是“The Rhône’s current was so gentle”，提取名词current即可。
定位时看准条件状语“hardly snowed...barely rained”，紧接着的主语就是你要找的答案。
It hardly snowed in the Alps that winter and that spring it barely rained. The Rhône’s current was so gentle that the team got in the water by early May.
题目问因为坏天气团队只损失了一个什么，原文说是“losing only a single week to bad weather”，提取名词week。
不要想当然地填成single，题目要的是具体的时间单位名词。
The team worked straight into November, losing only a single week to bad weather – and completed the job.
题目问船上装载了33吨的什么，原文明确写着“carrying 33 tons of stone”，直接填stone。
只要紧跟数字33，这个空基本不可能填错。
When Arles-Rhône 3 sank, it was carrying 33 tons of stone for building work.
题目问在木板下发现了一枚银质的什么，原文写的是“found a silver coin”，填写coin即可。
只要紧跟在修饰词silver后面的核心名词就是你要找的答案，非常直接。
When the restorers were taking the boat apart, they also found a silver coin sealed between two planks of wood; it had been put there to bring good luck.
